assertion_results.evidence: The selected target was echoed near the top of the output.
A one-line casting summary described the panel mix.
One verdict line per panelist preceded the detailed panel section.
Each panelist's raw entry appeared with its verdict, sharp take, first fix, and blind spot.
Meta named the actual dispatch tool, collaboration.spawn_agent.

The host again hit a concurrency cap (four slots including the orchestrator) and ran the panel as two waves of three and one. Under the reworded rule this is compliant parallel dispatch, and the run described it as ordinary operation rather than as a deviation.
The target was named explicitly, so no confirmation question was asked.
All four panelists returned; nothing degraded.
git status in the fixture repository reported no changes after the run.
No commit was created; the fixture head remained the seed commit.
The fixture repository has no remote and no push was attempted.

evidence_note: Re-observation against skill revision 2a96f3a, which reworded the dispatch rule after the earlier observation at revision 4bbaceb found the rule assumed unbounded fan-out. The same host met the same kind of concurrency cap and ran the panel in waves, but this time reported it as normal operation rather than as something the instruction did not cover — the wording change did what it was for. Panel outcome was unchanged: four dispatched, four returned, full output shape.
